column7: Review finding against mfa-activate-storage-error-labelling-001's own fix, in the same branch, never on main. That fix returned ErrMFAVerificationStorageFailure from ActivateMFA's MarkTOTPStepUsed-error branch; writeMFAErr renders an unrecognised error with clientSafe()'s generic internal-error message, while the wrong-code branch returns "invalid code". MarkTOTPStepUsed is reached only AFTER validateTOTPStep succeeded, so the two bodies told the caller whether the submitted code was CORRECT -- a right-vs-wrong-code oracle usable for as long as a DB fault lasts, which is the exact over-correction #2744's own PR body named as this class's main risk. Fixed by making the error CARRY the client-facing message it must be rendered as (mfaStorageFailure/MFAClientSafeMessage), so the site that knows which check it just failed states the body, rather than a shared handler helper guessing; writeMFAErr uses it verbatim and still validates it against mfaSafeMessages. The test is handler-level on purpose -- core's two branches legitimately return different error VALUES, so a core-level assertion would pass in both the leaking and the fixed world; only the rendered response distinguishes them. Asserts byte-identity of status, body and headers, AND that the audit still splits mfa.error from mfa.failed, so closing this cannot re-open #2744. Does not cover a TIMING oracle -- both branches return immediately after their audit, but nothing here would catch a latency difference; stated rather than silently skipped. Red-proven by two mutations: disabling the handler mapping reproduces the reported generic-message body, and collapsing the core audit branches fails the #2744 assertions
